drivers.text: The Dow gained 1,569 points to 53,356, its best day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,689. Investors read Democratic control of both chambers as gridlock that could limit the administration's agenda.

sowhat.text: Equities and credit are open for business, with HSBC selling $4.25B of bonds and megadeals like Marvell and Lumentum at ~$115B. But a 4.90% 10-year and about 81% odds of a December hike keep debt costly, so stock-funded buyers and infrastructure money have the edge.

pitch: The Dow jumped about 3 percent on Wednesday, its best day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent to about 7,689 after Democrats won both chambers of Congress and investors priced in gridlock. Oil fell more than 8 percent, with WTI at 88 dollars, on expectations of pressure to end the Iran war. The 10-year eased 5 basis points to 4.90 percent, but the market still puts about an 81 percent chance on a Fed hike on December 9. On deals, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for about 115 billion dollars in stock, and Blackstone and Canadian pensions are paying 3.1 billion dollars into LNG Canada.

quiz.q: Where did WTI crude settle on Wednesday 4 Nov?
Why did the Dow rise about 3% on Wednesday 4 Nov?
quiz.a: Democrats won control of the House and Senate, which investors read as political gridlock that could limit the administration's agenda. Oil also fell sharply, which helped sentiment.

quiz.q: How is Marvell paying for Lumentum?
quiz.a: All stock: 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, for an implied enterprise value of about $115B.

chat.a: The Dow jumped 3.0% to 53,356 on Wednesday, its best day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,689 after Democrats won Congress. Oil fell more than 8%, with WTI at $88.12. The 10-year eased to 4.90%, but a December Fed hike is still priced at about 81%.
chat.tip: Lead with the election and the gridlock read.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $88.12 and Brent at $94.62, each down about 8%, on expectations of pressure to end the Iran war. That is a big one-day move, and headlines can reverse it. Lower oil eases cost pressure for industrials but trims upstream cash flow, which can cool energy deal appetite.
chat.tip: Name the risk in both directions.

chat.a: Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock, a ~24% premium, with Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman on Marvell and Citi and Evercore on Lumentum. Blackstone and Canadian pensions are also paying $3.1B for 49.9% of Mitsubishi's holding company that owns a stake in LNG Canada.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The October jobs report on Friday 6 Nov, about +55K expected with unemployment at 4.2%, because it feeds the odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec, near 81% now. Also ConocoPhillips and Parker-Hannifin earnings Thursday as reads on energy and industrial demand.
chat.tip: Tie each event to the Fed or the energy theme.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.90% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Companies with most of their value in the terminal value fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: Why would a stock-funded deal like Marvell and Lumentum be attractive right now?
chat.a: Marvell is paying 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, a ~24% premium to 28 Oct prices. With the 10-year at 4.90% and a December hike priced at about 81%, debt is costly, so stock avoids borrowing. A fixed ratio shields both sides from relative moves but not from a sector selloff.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed target is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and futures price about an 81% chance of another on 9 Dec. The 10-year is 4.90%, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 340 bp on 3 Nov, and HSBC sold $4.25B of bonds, so markets are open.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
